brief.conference_theme: Environmental and social regeneration: beyond sustainability
brief.panel_theme: Circularity at scale: regenerative sourcing and supply chains

plan.summary: Build a three-person panel on circularity at scale, focusing on regenerative sourcing and supply chains in business. Favor rising or established, budget-conscious candidates with prior conference or presentation experience, and balance sectors, career stages, places, and organization types; national reach allows searches beyond New Haven.
plan.location_focus: National; include New Haven and the Northeast where useful

angles: Business-school and supply-chain researchers studying circular procurement, regenerative agriculture, and scaling reuse
Researchers presenting at circular economy and sustainable business conferences
Corporate sourcing, procurement, and supply-chain leaders implementing circular or regenerative practices
Circular-economy consultants and nonprofit program leaders with practical case studies and conference presentations
State or federal circular-economy, sustainable materials, and responsible-sourcing policy specialists
Think-tank policy experts on producer responsibility and circular supply chains who present to business audiences
Founders of early-stage circular materials, reuse, and regenerative sourcing businesses with demonstrated scale-up work
Small and mid-sized company leaders presenting supply-chain circularity case studies at industry events
Nonprofit and coalition leaders advancing just, regenerative supply chains and circular sourcing
Community or worker-centered advocates connecting materials circularity with equitable sourcing, with public speaking experience
Business or sustainability reporters covering circular supply chains, regenerative sourcing, and materials innovation
Trade-publication editors or podcast hosts who moderate circular economy and sustainable business discussions

cards.name: Kevin Lyons
cards.job_title: Professor of Professional Practice, Department of Supply Chain Management
cards.organization: Rutgers Business School–Newark and New Brunswick
cards.could_speak_on: How local sourcing, procurement criteria, and end-of-life analysis can help businesses build more regenerative and resilient supply chains.
talk_ideas: Embedding environmental and social criteria in procurement
Building local sourcing networks with community benefits
Using supply-chain archaeology to identify environmental impacts and end-of-life opportunities
cards.bio: Kevin Lyons is a professor of professional practice in supply chain management at Rutgers Business School and directs its Public Private Community Partnership Program. His research covers environmental, social, health, and economic criteria in supply-chain and procurement systems, including local sourcing and product end-of-life research.
credentials: Author of *Buying for the Future: Contract Management and the Environmental Challenge* and *A Roadmap to Green Supply Chains*.
cards.why_fit: He brings an academic and applied procurement perspective directly relevant to scaling social and environmental criteria and local sourcing across supply chains.

past_speaking.event: ARIS Summit keynote: “Supply Chains for Society: Quantifying Impact by Design”

notable_work: Developed the Supply Chain Archeology research discipline.
Research on local sourcing networks for anchor institutions and small businesses.
cards.fit_reason: Strong direct match on sourcing, procurement, supply-chain environmental and social criteria, plus a verified prior keynote.

cards.name: Vishal Agrawal
cards.job_title: Henry J. Blommer Family Endowed Chair in Sustainable Business; Professor of Operations and Information Management; Director, Business of Sustainability Initiative
cards.organization: Georgetown University, McDonough School of Business
cards.could_speak_on: How business-model innovation and sustainable operations can move circular sourcing from isolated initiatives toward wider adoption.
talk_ideas: Scaling sustainable business models through operations
Circularity in fashion and consumer-product systems
How business leaders and academics can collaborate on sustainable supply chains
cards.bio: Vishal Agrawal is the Henry J. Blommer Family Endowed Chair in Sustainable Business and a professor of operations and information management at Georgetown McDonough. He directs the university’s Business of Sustainability Initiative and has moderated speaker-series conversations on circularity, sustainable business, and supply chains.
cards.why_fit: He offers a business-school operations perspective and has experience moderating sustainability conversations that include circularity and supply-chain topics.

past_speaking.event: Business of Sustainability Initiative Speaker Series conversation with Danielle Solomon Nkojo on circularity and sustainability in fashion
Business of Sustainability Initiative Speaker Series conversation with Peter Blommer on supply chains and sustainable business practices

links.label: Business of Sustainability Initiative speaker series

cards.fit_reason: Relevant expertise in sustainable operations and documented moderation of conversations specifically about circularity and supply chains.

cards.could_speak_on: Scaling regenerative sourcing across international agricultural supply chains through traceability, supplier partnerships, and farmer-focused implementation.

Scaling responsible sourcing across crops and countries

credentials: Global Responsible Sourcing Lead for Vegetables and Spices, Nestlé
cards.why_fit: Provides a large-company sourcing perspective directly connected to regenerative agriculture and supply-chain implementation.

past_speaking.event: Regenerative Agriculture Forum 2026

cards.organization: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
cards.could_speak_on: Scaling circularity through product design, certification, and collaborative initiatives across supply chains and sectors.
talk_ideas: Circular design as a supply-chain strategy
Using product certification to advance circular sourcing
Cross-sector collaboration to scale safer, circular products

credentials: Senior Director of Strategy & Development, Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute

cards.name: Deborah Dull
cards.could_speak_on: Practical levers for embedding circularity in supply-chain strategy and operations, including how organizations can scale circular models.
talk_ideas: Four operational levers for circular supply chains
Moving from linear to circular sourcing and operations
Designing supply chains for material reuse and value retention
cards.bio: Deborah Dull founded the Circular Supply Chain Network and is Managing Partner of Trillium Digital Services. Her work spans supply-chain roles and organizations including Microsoft, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and General Electric; she has written books on circular and sustainable supply chains.
cards.why_fit: Directly aligned with circularity at scale and brings an operational supply-chain perspective, plus public speaking experience.

past_speaking.event: Circular Supply Chain Summit

cards.fit_reason: Her current work and expertise directly center on circular supply chains, with an evidenced summit appearance.

cards.name: Tom Ryan
cards.could_speak_on: Connecting farmers and downstream food companies through supply-chain value streams that support climate-smart agricultural practices.
talk_ideas: Creating value streams for farmers through supply-chain partnerships
From offsets to insets in agricultural supply chains
Scaling climate-smart practices through food and CPG partnerships
cards.bio: Tom Ryan is President of Truterra, Land O’Lakes’ sustainability business. His work focuses on connecting farmers, agricultural retailers, and food and consumer packaged goods companies to create supply-chain value streams and encourage climate-smart practices.
cards.why_fit: Brings an agribusiness implementation perspective linking farm adoption with downstream corporate sourcing demand.

past_speaking.event: The Modern Acre podcast: “From Offsets to Insets – Enabling a New Value Stream for Farmers”
2022 ARA Conference & Expo

cards.fit_reason: Strong practitioner fit at the farm-to-company interface, though his focus is regenerative agriculture more than circular materials.

cards.name: Mallory Anderson
cards.could_speak_on: How Minnesota’s packaging EPR law can shift producer responsibility, packaging design, and the systems needed for circular supply chains.
talk_ideas: What producer-funded packaging EPR means for sourcing and packaging choices
Designing reuse, recycling, and composting systems at statewide scale
Building producer accountability into packaging supply chains
cards.bio: Mallory Anderson is the Packaging EPR Coordinator at the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency. She leads implementation of Minnesota’s Packaging Waste and Cost Reduction Act, which establishes a producer-funded statewide packaging program.
cards.why_fit: Offers a direct state implementation perspective on how regulation and producer funding can influence packaging systems and business supply chains.

past_speaking.event: Beyond the Basics: Advancing EPR in the Great Lakes Region webinar
Project Optimist presentation on Minnesota’s EPR law
2025 EPR Think Tank

links.label: Product Stewardship Institute webinar speaker bio

cards.fit_reason: Strong match: her current state role centers on implementing packaging EPR, and multiple sources document public presentations on the topic.

cards.name: Daniel Zlatnik
cards.organization: California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle)
cards.could_speak_on: What packaging EPR and state plastics laws mean for producer obligations, business risk, and circular packaging systems.
talk_ideas: How state packaging EPR laws affect producers and supply-chain decisions
Regulatory approaches to plastic packaging and circularity
Navigating compliance and policy variation across states
cards.bio: Daniel Zlatnik is an attorney with CalRecycle, California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery. He has participated in public discussions on extended producer responsibility and state plastics and packaging laws.
cards.why_fit: Provides a legal and regulatory perspective on how packaging EPR laws shape producer obligations and business decisions.

past_speaking.event: People, Places, Planet podcast: “Packaged with Care: Plastic Packaging, EPR, and the Circular Economy”
Extended Producer Responsibility: Examining State Plastics and Packaging Laws
2025 EPR Think Tank

cards.name: Kara Steward
cards.job_title: Recycling Market Development Center Coordinator, Solid Waste Management Program
cards.could_speak_on: How public policy and market development can connect recovered materials to business supply chains and expand circular materials markets.
talk_ideas: Public-sector tools for growing markets for recycled materials
Connecting recycling infrastructure and recovered materials with manufacturers
How packaging policy implementation intersects with market development
cards.bio: Kara Steward works in the Solid Waste Management Program at the Washington State Department of Ecology and coordinates the state’s Recycling Market Development Center. Her work includes supporting implementation of Washington’s packaging extended producer responsibility program.
cards.why_fit: Brings a state-agency market-development perspective that complements packaging regulation with attention to demand, infrastructure, and material flows.

past_speaking.event: Clean Materials Policy in Washington webinar
2025 EPR Think Tank

links.label: Clean Materials Policy in Washington webinar

cards.name: Alysia Garmulewicz
cards.could_speak_on: How regenerative bio-based materials and open data can help shift sourcing and material innovation toward circular supply chains at scale.
talk_ideas: Scaling regenerative biomaterials with open data and AI
Regional renewable feedstocks and circular materials R&D
From scientific knowledge to commercial bio-based products
cards.bio: Alysia Garmulewicz is Co-CEO and Founder of Materiom, a platform providing open data and AI to accelerate bio-based materials development. She is also an associate professor focused on the circular economy at Universidad de Santiago de Chile and an associate fellow at the University of Oxford’s CABDyN Complexity Centre.
credentials: Doctorate from the Saïd Business School, University of Oxford
cards.why_fit: Her work directly connects regenerative biomaterials and materials R&D with the challenge of bringing new sourcing approaches toward wider use; her prior speaking includes circular economy and green chemistry sessions.

past_speaking.event: Circularity 25: “Green Chemistry as a Driver of Innovation” and “AI 2.0: Practical Tools for Circular Economy Leaders”
Ellen MacArthur Foundation Circular Economy Show, Episode 85: “Circular economy innovation: Regenerative materials in action”

notable_work: Materiom’s open data and AI platform for bio-based materials
cards.fit_reason: Strongest direct match to regenerative sourcing and materials innovation, with confirmed current founder role and multiple speaking appearances.

cards.name: Andy Ruben
cards.could_speak_on: How branded resale and reverse logistics can extend product life and reduce dependence on virgin materials across major retail supply chains.
talk_ideas: Scaling branded resale and trade-in across retail
Reverse logistics as circular supply-chain infrastructure
Aligning brand growth with lower reliance on new manufacturing
cards.bio: Andy Ruben is Founder and Executive Chairman of Trove, which partners with brands and retailers on branded resale and trade-in. Previously, he led sustainability efforts at Walmart as its first Chief Sustainability Officer and held roles in corporate and e-commerce strategy.
credentials: BS in Engineering and MBA, Washington University in St. Louis
Sam M. Walton Entrepreneur of the Year (2008)
cards.why_fit: He brings an industry-scale retail and reverse-logistics perspective, with experience in branded resale systems and prior public appearances as a speaker and podcast guest.

past_speaking.event: Circularity 25 keynote and sessions
Lead the Change podcast, “Andy Ruben on Revolutionizing Retail: A Deep Dive into Circularity and Innovation with Trove”

notable_work: Launched a branded resale platform for Patagonia in 2017
cards.fit_reason: A strong fit for the retail and reverse-logistics side of circularity at scale, with a confirmed current role and multiple speaking appearances.

cards.name: Tom Szaky
cards.could_speak_on: How businesses can build collection, recycling, and reusable-packaging systems with brand and retail partners as part of circular supply chains.
talk_ideas: Building reuse and collection systems with brand partners
The business models behind hard-to-recycle materials
When reuse can complement recycling in circular packaging
cards.bio: Tom Szaky is Founder and CEO of TerraCycle, a company focused on collecting and repurposing complex waste streams. TerraCycle’s Loop platform supports reusable packaging models, and Szaky is the author of several books on waste and packaging.
credentials: Author of Revolution in a Bottle, Outsmart Waste, Make Garbage Great, and The Future of Packaging
cards.why_fit: He can offer a founder’s view of creating collection and reusable-packaging systems with commercial partners. His confirmed current role and prior Aspen Ideas appearance establish relevant experience for a business-facing panel.

past_speaking.event: Aspen Ideas Festival 2022: “Ending the Plague of Plastic”
Sustainability In Your Ear podcast: “Tom Szaky On Building A Service-Centered Circular Economy”

cards.fit_reason: Relevant experience scaling commercial recycling and reuse models, though his focus is packaging and waste systems rather than regenerative sourcing specifically.

cards.name: Charles Kamenides
cards.could_speak_on: Community engagement and coalition-building to strengthen recycling systems and scale circular material flows.
talk_ideas: Building community partnerships for effective recycling systems
How coalitions can connect local recycling work to circularity at scale
Removing practical barriers to community participation in recycling
cards.bio: Charles Kamenides became Executive Director of the National Recycling Coalition in 2025. He brings more than 20 years of professional solid-waste management experience, including work in recycling and organics operations, business management, and program and policy development.
credentials: Over 20 years of professional solid-waste management experience
cards.why_fit: He can bring a national coalition perspective on how local participation, partnerships, and recycling-system operations contribute to circular material flows.

2026 National Recycling Congress member meeting: NRC 2.0
Circularity Forum 2026

cards.name: Robin Wiener
cards.could_speak_on: How recycled-materials industry advocacy and market infrastructure support dependable circular feedstocks for manufacturing supply chains.
talk_ideas: Making recycled materials reliable inputs for manufacturing
Industry advocacy and the systems needed to scale recycling markets
cards.bio: Robin Wiener is President of the Recycled Materials Association and serves as an advocate for the recycled-materials industry. ReMA represents companies that collect, process, broker, and consume recycled materials.
cards.why_fit: She offers a national trade-association perspective on the industry and advocacy conditions that can help recycled materials become viable supply-chain inputs.

past_speaking.event: REMADE 2025 Circular Economy Conference speakers

cards.fit_reason: Highly relevant to recycled feedstock and supply-chain circularity, with a confirmed current national industry role and one verified speaking appearance.

cards.why_fit: Her circular-economy expertise, supply-chain experience, and substantial record of talks align directly with a business-facing panel on regenerative sourcing at scale.

past_speaking.event: Corporate, academic, institute, trade, and public-sector talks (50+; individual event names not specified)
The Circular Economy Podcast

cards.name: Sheri R. Hinish

Circularity, climate finance, and just transition in supply chains

Supply Chain Revolution podcast episode on regenerative sourcing
